Grammar-derived bullets. StreamingPatchParser::finish() returns the collected hunk vector with no minimum-count check, so the bare marker pair parses to zero hunks; the 'empty patch' rejection belongs to assess_patch_safety, not the parser.
Install channels and archive names come from the README at the pinned commit; the Node.js floor is the published package's engines field (>=16 at 0.170.0), which corrects the earlier '18+' claim.
Comment states the published engines floor (>=16), verified from the npm registry metadata for 0.170.0; the earlier '18+' comment was wrong.

Revision notice: the five withdrawn usage figures are named as withdrawn rather than silently dropped, and the correction pass is disclosed in the article. No figure in the block is presented as a current measurement.

Counted from the enum body at cc7a62e: 66 variants, from Model through MemoryUpdate. The article now says the table is a selection of eleven and not the enum, and each quoted description was matched verbatim against the description() method in the same file read. Round-2 review recounted 66 variants and matched all eleven description() strings, including the /mcp string, in the fresh file.
No Approval, Context, Commit or Reset variant exists among the 66 variants at cc7a62e, so the four earlier command names are genuinely absent and the removal claim holds.

All eleven rows re-checked at cc7a62e: command names and description() strings exist as quoted, including /mcp 'list MCP tools; /mcp verbose or /mcp login <name> [--environment <id>]', which replaces the earlier paraphrase. Round-2 review recounted 66 variants and matched all eleven description() strings, including the /mcp string, in the fresh file.

assess_patch_safety auto-approves only when the patch is constrained to writable paths AND (PermissionProfile::Disabled|External OR sandbox_available); the source comment states those two profiles intentionally apply no outer sandbox. Both rejection strings are the constants declared at the top of safety.rs. Round-2 review re-read assess_patch_safety: the Disabled/External disjunct and the no-outer-sandbox comment are present as described.

The bullet states only the two auto-approve branches read from safety.rs; the hard-link caveat is the source comment's own reasoning and the article no longer claims a sandbox runs in the Disabled/External case. Round-2 review re-read assess_patch_safety: the Disabled/External disjunct and the no-outer-sandbox comment are present as described.

evidence_boundary: Source and vendor-reference reading only, at one pinned commit (cc7a62e): parser grammar and tests, crate root, assess_patch_safety, the approval adapter, one per-model prompt file, the TUI slash-command enum, the README, and the configuration reference, plus the installed CLI's help text. No patch was applied and no Codex session was run; the grammar illustration is labelled a hand-built payload.
proposed_process_improvements: The research brief declared the approval-mode matrix out of scope because core/src/safety.rs was not fetched in the research attempt; the write stage fetched it in one call (~2 s) and the article is materially better for it. Stage briefs should fetch one obvious follow-up file rather than shipping a known gap.

Legacy sections of a refreshed article (CLI flags, config keys, slash commands) are not re-verified by the research stage, and this refresh found --approval-mode flags that the installed CLI does not have. Refresh briefs should include a one-command check of the current --help output for any guide whose body contains CLI invocations.

Correction round 1 found errors of the exact class the round-0 receipts could not catch: legacy sections (install URLs, config tables, slash commands, plan names) inherited from the pre-refresh article were carried forward without re-reading a primary source. A refresh brief should require one source check per legacy section that makes a verifiable claim, not only for the new section.

A correction payload that names the failing items is worth its tokens: R1-R9 each pointed at a specific string, which made a 30-minute re-check possible. Prefer this shape over a general 'reviewer disagrees' note.

A table presented as 'the enum' should be validated by counting variants in the source, not by checking each row against its own description: every row matched while the scope sentence was still false. Add a count-the-collection check to the write stage for any partial listing (commands, flags, config keys, plan tiers).

When a source comment explains one branch of a boolean, quote the branch structure from the code expression itself. Round 1 paraphrased the sandbox comment as the whole condition and dropped the PermissionProfile::Disabled|External disjunct that the same expression carries.

items: Title and description changed to the assigned selection title (apply_patch mechanics) and mirrored in the schema partial headline/description.
Withdrew five unverifiable usage figures and named them in a revision note instead of restating them.

Replaced the `--approval-mode suggest|auto-edit|full-auto` examples, which the installed codex-cli 0.170.0 help output does not list, with -a/--ask-for-approval and -s/--sandbox combinations; the FAQ wording and the context-window row were adjusted to match.
Removed the 'Pre-Commit Code Review Subagent' subsection: its [git] pre_commit_review keys could not be verified and are not present in the pinned source read.
R1: the hunk-minimum bullet now says the grammar requires hunk+ while the parser accepts a bare marker pair as zero hunks, and that assess_patch_safety rejects the empty action with 'empty patch'.
R2: dropped the untrusted-variant clause; -a lists only on-request and never, 'codex -a untrusted' is an argument error, and the reference says untrusted is unsupported.
R3: Homebrew command corrected to 'brew install --cask codex' per the README at the pinned commit.
R4: removed the 404 binary URL; the Linux path now uses the README's install.sh and names the codex-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz archive.

R5: replaced the invented [defaults]/[sandbox]/[approval_policies] tables and context_window key with the documented model, approval_policy, model_context_window, sandbox_mode and [sandbox_workspace_write] keys, and named the removed keys.
R6: MCP config now uses the documented mcp_servers.<id>.* table form instead of [[mcp_servers]] with a name key.
R7: slash-command table rebuilt from tui/src/slash_command.rs at the pinned commit; /approval, /context, /commit and /reset removed, and /model documented as a picker with no argument.
R8: plan list is Plus, Pro, Business, Edu, Enterprise per the README.
R9: removed the 'Auto Edit mode' comment that contradicted this page's own flag correction.

Extra check: the 'Node.js 18+' prerequisite was wrong — the published package declares engines node >=16 at version 0.170.0 (npm registry metadata), so both the prose and the code comment now say 16+.

C1: the slash-command section no longer calls its eleven rows 'the command enum'. It states the enum declares 66 variants and that the table is a selection, names description() as the source of each quoted string, and replaces the /mcp paraphrase with the file's own string 'list MCP tools; /mcp verbose or /mcp login <name> [--environment <id>]'. The earlier-names sentence now says 'among the enum's 66 variants'.

C2: the paragraph after the decision table now states both auto-approve branches (sandbox available, or PermissionProfile::Disabled/External which intentionally apply no outer sandbox), quotes the source comment that names the second branch, and records that the writable-path helper short-circuits to true under a full-disk policy.

C2 follow-through: the approval-adapter bullet no longer says 'the prompt is skipped, the sandbox is not'; it says the prompt is skipped and the patch is not flagged to bypass the sandbox, with the outer sandbox left to the permission profile.

C2 follow-through: the Practical Consequences bullet now says AutoApprove has two branches and that in the Disabled/External branch no outer sandbox backstops the path check, instead of claiming every auto-approved patch runs inside a sandbox.

Independently re-verified at cc7a62e: 66 enum variants counted from the body, all eleven description strings matched verbatim, no Approval/Context/Commit/Reset variant, and slash_command.rs (98f0dfa1...) / safety.rs (e51f6625...) / apply_patch.rs (f37e3773...) hashes identical to the saved raw records. No article claim rests on unread source.
